premises.text: Kids need taught digital engagement like driving; incumbent social media exposes them to predatory algorithms, addiction loops, strangers, data risks, and inappropriate content
premises.evidence_span: social media has some challenges, like predatory algorithms, addictive behavioral loops that reinforce toxic mindsets, strangers and creepers, not the Minecraft kind, sliding into DMs, compromised personal data, and inappropriate videos and messaging

premises.text: Betweened supports kids' digital literacy with kid-friendly creator tools, co-creation, guided authentic profiles, and socially appropriate communication
premises.evidence_span: Betweened is a platform that will support kids' digital literacy while providing the entertainment and education, the interaction that they crave

premises.text: Parental tools and guided curriculum customize features by age/stage so kids unlock capabilities progressively
premises.evidence_span: we provide parental tools that can be turned on and off, because kids shouldn't have access to all of the tools right off the bat

premises.text: Expert-curated, moderated, age-appropriate content with pause moments and verified parental consent ensures privacy-compliant kid feed
premises.evidence_span: all of that content is there for the kids, and it is curated and moderated by experts, by adults trained in developmental psychology and in our editorial guidelines

premises.text: Beta starts with content to jumpstart engagement/network effects, then invites and brand partnerships grow the family network
premises.evidence_span: we're intentionally starting with content for our beta, because this addresses a major pain point for parents, age-appropriate content. But it also ensures that Between is engaging from the start, allowing us to jumpstart network effects

value.text: Mindful, responsible social media that teaches kids to engage and disengage thoughtfully
value.evidence_span: building mindful, responsible social media for kids and families

causal_links.evidence_span: They need to be taught how to engage and how to disengage with technology
everything that is on the platform is appropriate for kids
course correct social media for kids around the world

notes: Pain list (algorithms, addiction, strangers, data, inappropriate content) folded into one P1 problem-set per v1.5.1 rule 6. Creator tools, co-creation, profiles, and troll curriculum folded into P2 as facets of the literacy/entertainment platform. Founder biography and fundraising ask excluded. Brands' kid-purchasing market framing not coded as a separate premise.
